limits: The full canonical image archive and raw canonical database were not retained (no encrypted database artifact exists for this run). Canonical identity and projected-byte hashes come from the authenticated CI security artifact.

The tpm2-tss profiles and magic.mgc of the replay are byte-identical to the canonical files and to the files reviewed on 2026-11-08, so those four findings are carried over unchanged. The replay database and its projection differ from the canonical ones (8 of the nine database regions keep their projection lines and 1 moves), but the complete match bytes, lengths and SHA-256 digests agree, so the structural interpretation applies to the replay and binds to the canonical scanner bytes through the complete span digests.

A freeblock's content is the remainder of a deleted index record: its key and integer rowid bytes after the four header bytes the freeblock overwrote. Each such remainder equals the key and rowid of one live row of the immutable base database, a fedora-gpg-keys 44-1 file, and its key is a complete live key of the current database. Where the detector's candidate extends past a filename, the extra bytes are that record's rowid.
Only hashes, coordinates and structural metadata are retained publicly. Candidate values, filenames and raw scanner matches remain private.
Every finding outside these exact complete regions remains blocking. Owner swiftraccoon and expiry 2026-11-29 are unchanged; no path, package or rule exemption and no expiry renewal.
The observed image scan failed. A fresh canonical image gate is required before signing or deployment, and the Fedora repositories may move again before that build.
